Mike Nolan, chief executive officer, said, "Our Title business delivered another strong quarter, generating adjusted pre-tax title earnings of $422 million and an industry leading adjusted pre-tax title margin of 17.1%. These results reflect the strength of our disciplined operating strategy and our ability to consistently outperform the broader market. Commercial remained a meaningful contributor, with revenue increasing 19% over the prior year, while our residential purchase business continued to outperform despite low transaction volumes. As we manage through this market cycle, we remain focused on maintaining our operating discipline and investing in the business to drive long-term growth and profitability."
Revenue growth

Insurers earn revenue three ways. The core insurance business itself, often called underwriting and represented in the income statement as premiums earned, is one way. Investment income from investing the “float” (premiums collected upfront not yet paid out as claims) in assets such as fixed-income assets and equities is the second way. Fees from various sources such as policy administration, annuities or other value-added services are the third. Fidelity National Financial struggled to consistently increase demand as its $14.91 billion of revenue for the trailing 12 months was close to its revenue five years ago. That underwhelming result suggests it is a low-quality business.

Long-term growth matters most, but within financials, a half-decade historical view may miss recent interest rate changes, market returns and industry trends. Fidelity National Financial’s annualized revenue growth of 5.1% over the last two years is above its five-year trend, a positive sign.

children: Note: Quarters not shown were determined to be outliers because they were impacted by outsized investment gains/losses that are not indicative of the recurring fundamentals of the business.
This quarter, Fidelity National Financial missed Wall Street’s consensus estimates and reported an uninspiring 11.2% year-on-year revenue decline, generating $3.58 billion of revenue.

Net premiums earned made up 43.9% of the company’s total revenue during the last five years, meaning Fidelity National Financial’s growth reflects a balance between insurance and non-insurance activities.

image.alt: Fidelity National Financial quarterly net premiums earned as % of revenue

children: Net premiums earned command greater market attention due to their reliability and consistency, whereas investment and fee income are often seen as more volatile revenue streams that fluctuate with market conditions.
Net premiums earned

When insurers sell policies, they protect themselves from unusually large losses or an outsized accumulation of losses with reinsurance (insurance for insurance companies). Net premiums earned are calculated as follows:
Gross premiums - what’s ceded to reinsurers as a risk mitigation and transfer strategy

Fidelity National Financial’s net premiums earned have declined by 4.5% annually over the last five years, much worse than the broader insurance industry. This shows that policy underwriting underperformed its other business lines.

Fidelity National Financial’s net premiums earned growth accelerated to 16.1% annually over the last two years. Net premiums earned outpaced total revenue over this period, implying that other line items such as investment income grew at a slower rate. These additional streams do play a key role in the bottom line, but their impact can vary. While some firms have excelled in consistently investing their float, sudden shifts in the fixed income and equity markets can significantly affect short-term performance.

children: Key takeaways from Fidelity National Financial’s Q3 results

With revenue below Wall Street’s consensus estimates and EPS in line, Fidelity National Financial’s Q3 results offered few positives and amounted to a weaker quarter. Shares rose 3% to $44.20 immediately after the release.
When assessing Fidelity National Financial at its current price, it’s important to consider its valuation, business qualities and latest quarterly results.
